letters.title: John Overton to Andrew Jackson
letters.author: John Overton
letters.credit: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, Andrew Jackson Papers. Series 1, General Correspondence and Related Items, 1775-1885; MSS 27532, Vol. 82.
letters.catalogNote: The LoC item record gives the extent as "3 pages"; the digitized resource (maj.01082_0068_0071) holds four image files, 0068-0071, and all four are held here. Looking at the images: 0068 is the first page of the letter (folio stamp 16281); 0069 is the second and last page, with the signature; 0070 is a second microfilm frame of the same opening, showing the blank facing side of the second leaf (folio stamp 16282) with the right-hand edge of page 2 at the left margin; 0071 is the outer side of the second leaf, carrying a four-line filing endorsement and a cropped trace of the address panel. So the letter text occupies two pages; "3 pages" most plausibly counts the three inscribed sides (two of text plus the endorsement), and the fourth image adds no writing. That reading of the count is an inference, not an LoC statement. The existing held file originals/overton-letter.jpg is byte-identical to 0068.jpg (same SHA-256).
letters.summary: Modern commentary: Writing from Travellers Rest, Overton encloses a copy of "Mr Poinsetts speech" (identified by the edition as Joel R. Poinsett's Charleston speech of October 5, 1832, against nullification) and tells Jackson that no man but he can calm Southern feeling over the tariff. He expects Jackson's re-election to allay the heat he blames on Calhoun, and an armed vessel guarding the federal revenue to do what that does not. He adds that the cotton crop is poor, 21,000 picked from 80 acres with rain falling, and closes with a prayer for Jackson's health.

edition.citation: Daniel Feller, Thomas Coens, and Laura-Eve Moss, eds., The Papers of Andrew Jackson, Volume X, 1832 (Knoxville: University of Tennessee Press, 2016), p. 553, "From John Overton" (source line: ALS, DLC (41)).
edition.note: Used as the base text (open-access PDF, DOI 10.7290/utp5209), then read against the manuscript images line by line. The edition's wording was confirmed throughout except one word in the closing (see page 2). Line breaks, the dashes Overton wrote where the edition prints full stops, the colon in the signature and the foot-of-page addressee line follow the manuscript; capitalization of ambiguous letterforms follows the edition. The LoC item and resource JSON carry no transcription. The letter is not printed in John Spencer Bassett, ed., Correspondence of Andrew Jackson, vol. 4, 1829-1832 (Carnegie Institution, 1929): its Internet Archive full text was searched for the opening words and key phrases without result. Founders Online/Rotunda and HathiTrust were not searched.

letters.catalogNote: LoC record confirmed from its JSON: title "John Overton to Andrew Jackson, June 2, 1831", Overton as author, Jackson as correspondent, extent "3 pages", four image files 0001-0004. The images show a signed statement rather than a dated letter: 0001 is page 1 (folio stamp 15173); 0002 is page 2, three lines, the signature and the addressee line; 0003 is the blank inner side of the second leaf (folio stamp 15174) with show-through; 0004 is the outer panel with the address and Jackson's filing endorsement. As with the 1832 letter, three inscribed sides and four images. Overton wrote no date or place: the date comes from Jackson's endorsement ("2nd. of June 1831"), repeated in a later pencil note at the top of page 1, and the edition brackets it as [Jun 2]. The place is an inference: A. J. Donelson's certified copy (LoC maj024467) is headed "Statement of Judge Overton's made at Washington 2d of June 1831", and Bassett prints the heading as "[Washington ?]".
letters.summary: Modern commentary: A signed statement Overton gave Jackson about the Seminole War of 1818. He recalls that when he wrote a pamphlet defending the campaign, Jackson showed him his confidential letter to President Monroe and a letter from John Rhea conveying the President's approval, that Jackson later said he had destroyed Rhea's letter at Rhea's request, and that Overton had warned him the War Department's "carte Blanche" order might be used against him. Jackson endorsed it to be carefully preserved.

edition.citation: Daniel Feller, Laura-Eve Moss, Thomas Coens, and Erik B. Alexander, eds., The Papers of Andrew Jackson, Volume IX, 1831 (Knoxville: University of Tennessee Press, 2013), p. 282, "From John Overton" (source line: ADS, DLC (39)).
edition.note: Used as the base text (open-access PDF, DOI 10.7290/utp9109) and read against the manuscript images line by line; the wording agrees throughout. The edition also prints Jackson's endorsement and the address, both used to check the outer panel. Line breaks and the foot-of-page addressee line follow the manuscript. The statement is also printed, with abbreviations expanded, in John Spencer Bassett, ed., Correspondence of Andrew Jackson, vol. 4 (Carnegie Institution, 1929), pp. 287-288, headed "[Washington ?], June 2, 1831"; its wording agrees.

letters.catalogNote: LoC record confirmed from its JSON: title "John Overton to Andrew Jackson, August 25, 1827", Overton as author, Jackson as correspondent, extent "4 pages", four image files 0334-0337; here the count and the images agree. 0334 is page 1; 0335 is page 2; 0336 is page 3, six lines, the close and signature; 0337 is the address panel. The images confirm the signature (Jno: Overton), the addressee (Genl A Jackson at the foot of page 3; "Genl Andrew Jackson, Hermitage near Nashville" on the address panel) and the dateline "Sparta Augt 25th 1827". One thing is unresolved: the manuscript postmark on the address panel reads "Sparta T / Augt 23rd" on my reading, two days before the date LoC and the Papers of Andrew Jackson calendar give; the day numeral in the dateline is cramped and could be read 23 or 25. The LoC date is kept.
letters.summary: Modern commentary: Writing from Sparta, Overton tells Jackson that Judge Isacks has given him a note about "Clays bargain and management" of the presidential election of January 1825, with a copy for Jackson that he will bring home rather than post. He and Isacks think it improper to publish it for now, and he says that no one doubts Jackson's statement; the close, which names Buchanan and Markley, calls it an important paper in "perfect confirmation of what has been stated". Only the opening and the close are transcribed here; the calendar of the Papers of Andrew Jackson identifies the judge as Jacob C. Isacks.

edition.citation: Harold D. Moser and J. Clint Clifft, eds., The Papers of Andrew Jackson, Volume VI, 1825-1828 (Knoxville: University of Tennessee Press, 2002), Calendar, p. 592 (calendar entry only: "From John Overton. ALS, DLC (34). Reports obtaining statement from Jacob C. Isacks, confirming AJ's account of James Buchanan's role in the 1825 election, and discusses the likelihood of Buchanan's making a statement.").
edition.note: No published full text was found: the edition lists this letter in its calendar with a one-sentence summary and does not print it. The summary was used only to confirm author, repository and subject. The transcription was made directly from the images.

letters.summary: Modern commentary: A short letter about money. Overton has to meet a $1,000 draft at the bank and, having no cash in hand, asks Jackson for a bank credit of $429.40, the balance Jackson still holds out of $1,350 after paying out $920.60. A receipt signed by Overton at the foot, dated 22 January 1812, records that he received the sum in a check on the Nashville bank.

edition.citation: Harold D. Moser and Sharon Macpherson, eds., The Papers of Andrew Jackson, Volume II, 1804-1813 (Knoxville: University of Tennessee Press, 1984), Calendar, p. 564 (calendar entry only: "Jan 19 From John Overton. ALS, DLC. Requests a loan of money.").
edition.note: No published full text was found: the edition lists this letter in its calendar with a four-word summary and does not print it. The entry was used only to confirm author, date and repository. The transcription was made directly from the images.
